facts.text: Hilmar-Irwin was founded in 1984 by 12 dairy families, and the Hilmar Cheese Company remains the town’s most recognizable landmark.
The town’s layout splits into eastern and western halves along Lander Avenue, with historic 1920s homes on the east side and newer midcentury houses on the west.
A family‑owned bakery on Main Street, the Hilmar Portuguese Bakery, serves traditional sweet bread and cookies, while its adjoining fish market offers fresh Portuguese seafood.
Every October, Irwin Acres hosts a pumpkin patch that features a mini haunted house, a corn maze, tractor rides, and pony rides for families.
Hilmar-Irwin sits in northern Merced County at 37°24′30″N 120°51′3″W, about 6 miles west‑southwest of Delhi and 6 miles south of Turlock.
The climate brings hot, mostly dry summers and cool, wet winters, with January highs averaging 54°F and lows around 40°F.
